keyVerseText: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. of Christ: or, for Christ
rootMeaning: The Greek verb ἀποβλέπω (apoblépō) is formed from the prefix ἀπό (apó), meaning 'away from,' and the root βλέπω (blépō), meaning 'to look.' Together, they convey the literal sense of looking away from all else toward a single object. This root meaning emphasizes a focused, intentional gaze, far beyond a casual glance, highlighting a deliberate act of paying close attention or giving respect.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Hebrews 11:26, where it is translated as 'he had respect.' This consistent translation reflects the idea of looking intently or regarding something with deep consideration and value. The singular occurrence suggests a precise and weighty use, emphasizing intentional regard rather than a general or casual look.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀποβλέπω enriches our grasp of biblical faith as a deliberate and focused trust in God and Christ. It conveys more than mere awareness; it implies a steadfast attention and valuation of divine promises and rewards above worldly things. This word invites believers to fix their gaze unwaveringly on Christ, embodying a faith that chooses to regard Him as supremely valuable, even in the face of reproach or sacrifice. Such intentional looking is foundational for a life of faith that esteems eternal realities over temporal gain.
keyVerseReflection: Hebrews 11:26 declares that Moses esteemed the reproach of Christ as greater riches than the treasures of Egypt, 'for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.' The use of ἀποβλέπω here underscores Moses' deliberate and focused regard toward the future reward promised by God. It highlights that his faith was not passive but an active, intentional looking away from worldly wealth toward the eternal reward in Christ, demonstrating the essence of faith as a purposeful orientation of the heart.
